strings.name: Terence Tao
strings.role: Mathematician · Researcher in harmonic analysis and number theory
strings.summary: Terence Tao is an Australian-born mathematician and longtime UCLA professor. He connects methods from harmonic analysis, number theory, combinatorics and partial differential equations. With Ben Green he proved that primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions, and he solved the Erdős discrepancy problem. A 2006 Fields medallist, he also shares mathematics through blogging and open collaboration.

strings.influence.rationale: He contributed to harmonic analysis, number theory and partial differential equations, among other fields, and influences mathematical research and education through open exchange.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Green–Tao theorem
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: With Ben Green, proved that primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions, connecting number theory and combinatorics.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Analysis and open collaboration
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Works across analysis and partial differential equations, encouraging exchange through his blog and Polymath collaborations.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Appointed Companion of the Order of Australia
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Appointed a Companion of the Order of Australia in the King's Birthday Honours for contributions including mathematical research.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Solves Erdős discrepancy problem
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Proved the longstanding discrepancy conjecture, also drawing on an argument developed through the earlier Polymath5 collaboration.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Receives Waterman Award
strings.timeline.event-3.text: The US National Science Foundation awarded him the Waterman Award, supporting his research across several areas of mathematics.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Receives Fields Medal
strings.timeline.event-4.text: The International Mathematical Union recognized his work in partial differential equations, combinatorics, harmonic analysis and additive number theory.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Proves prime progression theorem with Green
strings.timeline.event-5.text: With Ben Green, established arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions in the primes; the paper was published in 2008.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Completes Princeton doctorate
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Completed doctoral work under Elias Stein and joined UCLA's mathematics department the same year.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Completes Flinders degrees
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Completed undergraduate and master’s studies as a teenager, then moved to Princeton for further mathematical training.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Born in Adelaide
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Born and raised in Australia, received accelerated mathematical education and later won medals at the International Mathematical Olympiad.
